ATTACHED MANUEL ACADEMY LEARNER RESOURCE

Resource ID: ma-resource:ma-g12-arts-and-music-u02-l03

Lesson focus: portfolio and application materials

Resource type: ACADEMY_CREATED_SCAFFOLD

GUIDED SCAFFOLD A — first supported pass for portfolio and application materials. 1 INTENT: name what the study should do. 2 SETUP: choose a safe, available route. 3 NOTICE: locate purpose, milestone, artifact record, decision trail, rights note, criteria check, and next step. 4 ACT: complete one small study using this cue—Selection and sequencing create an argument about growth or purpose; process evidence makes revisions and authorship traceable without continuous surveillance. 5 CHECK: point to the result before using “works” or “does not work.” 6 SECOND STUDY: change one relationship only. Keep both attempts and circle the exact prompt you are ready to remove. Worked example for portfolio and application materials: A three-item sequence—question, experiment, revision—can reveal a clearer process than ten unrelated polished pieces. Use it to study portfolio and application materials; describe evidence before judging and adapt the demonstrated relationship rather than copying a finished work.

How to use it: Use the attached Academy-created guided scaffold for both supported studies, then mark the prompt you are ready to remove.

Rights: Manuel Academy original; licensed CC BY 4.0 for learner use and adaptation. No third-party text, image, score, lyric, melody, recording, or performance is included.

Access and materials: Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
critique_criteria: The submission contains the required work blocks and one reviewable process state; each required artifact, study, response, or process note can be located.

The learner locates relevant purpose, milestone, artifact record, decision trail, rights note, criteria check, and next step and explains how the evidence relates to the stated intent, claim, or criterion.
The learner states an intent or claim and supports it with observable evidence while retaining ownership of artistic decisions.
The process record shows a check and a learner-chosen revision or reasoned decision to keep the result.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available for spoken reflection, explanation, or critique and scores the same. Use a written analysis, labelled plan, evidence table, notation, diagram, or private artifact check that preserves the stated target. No microphone, camera, recording, or public audience is required.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
For any multi-session project, supply a written milestone plan, checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown, so executive-function load is not silently part of what is being assessed.

Adjust quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode while holding the target constant. Where the target names a specific skill, change how it is evidenced rather than substituting a different skill.

Accept typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, notated, constructed, or demonstrated responses. Where performance is the target, a private demonstration to one trusted adult carries the same weight as any audience, and requires no recording.
Provide adaptive instruments and grips, enlarged or braille notation, seated and standing studio access, low-odour and low-dust material substitutes, and hearing protection on request.

Where documentation quality is itself the target, document the artwork alone with no person in frame, or have an adult verify the physical work directly. Neither route requires an image of the learner, and both preserve the documentation target rather than replacing it.
task_accessibility_provisions: Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Public performance is never required. A private, low-audience, or written-and-scored alternative always carries the same academic target.
No recording of the learner’s voice, no photograph, and no video is ever required; documentation may be written, notated, sketched, or adult-verified instead.
Use only original, public-domain, licensed, or family-approved works. Do not reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or other protected works without documented rights.
The tutor may explain technique, ask diagnostic questions, and critique work, but never silently completes graded creative work.

media.fallback: Use the complete supplied beat map, script, evidence record, or event description. No teacher handout or outside search is required.

remediation: Route 1: Reduce portfolio and application materials to three locatable events, areas, steps, or decisions. Label the intended effect beside each and underline the one purpose relationship that should carry it. Use a separate small study, four-event loop, thumbnail, evidence table, or paper plan. The adult may model the noticing process on different material but may not change the learner’s work. Check yourself: Point to or name the exact purpose evidence before deciding whether it serves the intent. New attempt: Put the support away and make a new arrangement, passage, response, or plan; record what the new evidence shows. Route 2: Return to the last understandable state. Hold every relationship steady except one chosen feature from purpose, milestone, artifact record, decision trail, rights note, criteria check, and next step; predict what that single change should do. Test the feature on scrap paper, a silent count, a two-event rehearsal loop, movable shapes, or a short evidence sentence before changing the scored work. Check yourself: Name what stayed the same, what changed, and the first observable result—without using “better” as the evidence. New attempt: Create a different small case using the same one-variable method, then transfer the finding to the original task only if it serves the learner’s intent.
extension: Apply portfolio and application materials under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or explain the idea to someone else using an original example. Treat this as optional depth on portfolio and application materials rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.

concept_registry.meaning: A portfolio or project is a purposeful sequence of work and decisions, not simply a pile of finished pieces.
The relationship among artistic intent, observable purpose, milestone, artifact record, decision trail, rights note, criteria check, and next step, and a criteria-based conclusion.

technique_registry.meaning: Isolate and test one purpose relationship while working on portfolio and application materials.
Record observable evidence before judging, then choose or decline a revision with a reason.
Use a bounded study, loop, excerpt, map, or prototype to test one relationship without demanding polish.

age_policy.language: Portfolio-ready disciplinary language with limitations and decisions stated precisely.
age_policy.safety: Use familiar low-risk materials, stop or adjust any physical or sound action that causes discomfort, and require adult help for cutting, heat, fumes, or heavy equipment.
age_policy.privacy: Private work and self-critique carry full credit; no public display, identifiable media, account, or recording is required.

a bounded checkpoint with reviewable evidence

concept_instruction.title: What portfolio and application materials means here
concept_instruction.body: A portfolio or project is a purposeful sequence of work and decisions, not simply a pile of finished pieces.

concept_instruction.title: How the relationship changes the result
concept_instruction.body: Selection and sequencing create an argument about growth or purpose; process evidence makes revisions and authorship traceable without continuous surveillance.

concept_instruction.title: Choice and tradeoff
concept_instruction.body: More items can show range but weaken focus. Fewer items can create coherence but must provide enough evidence for the stated goal. Worked example: A three-item sequence—question, experiment, revision—can reveal a clearer process than ten unrelated polished pieces. Non-example: Choosing only favourites without criteria does not explain why the group belongs together.

technique_sequence.action: State the intended effect or question before making or judging.
technique_sequence.notice: The statement creates a criterion that can be checked.
technique_sequence.why: Arts evidence is interpreted in relation to purpose, not personal taste.

technique_sequence.action: Identify or set up the relevant purpose, milestone, artifact record, decision trail, rights note, criteria check, and next step.
technique_sequence.notice: Locate the first relationship that can be observed in portfolio and application materials.
technique_sequence.why: Selection and sequencing create an argument about growth or purpose; process evidence makes revisions and authorship traceable without continuous surveillance.

technique_sequence.action: Complete one small controlled study or rehearsal loop.
technique_sequence.notice: Keep most relationships stable so one decision remains readable.
technique_sequence.why: A bounded test makes cause and effect easier to notice.

technique_sequence.action: Transfer the idea to a fresh work, excerpt, source detail, or project decision.
technique_sequence.notice: Close the model or cue before the independent decision.

technique_sequence.action: Check against criteria and choose a revision or a reasoned decision to keep the result.
technique_sequence.notice: Cite a location, moment, event, or process fact before judging.
technique_sequence.why: Evidence protects creative variation and learner authority.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: The stated intent for portfolio and application materials is present, but the record does not yet locate purpose, milestone, artifact record, decision trail, rights note, criteria check, and next step that supports it.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The learner supports a different, ambiguous, subtle, or intentionally open effect with observable evidence.

common_technique_errors.observable_mismatch: Several relationships changed at once, so the learner cannot yet tell which choice caused the observed effect.
common_technique_errors.not_an_error_when: The task is an intentionally exploratory diagnostic and no causal claim is being scored.
